messages.text:
another session reports that it has the spawn tool in the catalog even though i started it (like this one) with subagents=None, pls investigate

goal is that we expose a handful of tools (send_message, request_review) to all sessions, the other agents tools we only expose when subagents=Mjolnir
I’ll trace how the agents tool catalog is built and filtered, then fix the exposure rule and test it.

I found the cause: enabling push reviews forces the session’s MCP role to `Parent`, which exposes `spawn`, `list_agents`, and `close` even with `subagents=None`. I’m using the mj skill’s tool guidance here. The fix will make review tools independent of delegation permissions.

The daemon rejects `spawn` under `None`, so the permission check works; the catalog and instructions are wrong. That also prevents delegation for this fix, so I’ll complete it locally. Sessions without Mjolnir sub-agents will keep messaging, fetch, and configured review tools.

The fix now preserves the role selected by `subagents` and adds review tools separately. I’ve updated both profile registration and ACP delivery. The regressions check the advertised tools, rejection of hidden delegation tools, and review calls from sessions without delegation.
Workspace Clippy passed. The live launch file confirms this session has `subagents=None` and push reviews enabled, matching the defect exactly. The full core and worker test suites are still running.

The new regressions passed: push reviews no longer change `None` or `Native` into a delegation role, and review calls work from the restricted role. The remaining worker tests are still running; then I’ll commit, request review, and push.
The full core and worker suites passed, along with workspace Clippy and formatting. Commit `c5e89cf12` is ready and the required review is running. I’ll push to `origin/master` once it clears.

Found and fixed: push reviews incorrectly granted the full delegation tool catalog under `subagents=None`.

Commit `c5e89cf12` separates review tools from delegation permissions. Tests, Clippy, and formatting passed. Required review is pending; I’ll push when it clears.

Both reviewers caught a remaining restriction: `request_review` is still tied to the push gate. I’ll make it available with every top-level tool catalog and keep the push setting responsible for enforcement and instructions.

The daemon also rejects requests unless the trigger is `Push`. I’ll remove that restriction for explicit review requests, so `request_review` works end to end when automatic reviews are off or run after turns.

The follow-up now puts `request_review` in the common top-level tool catalog, independent of the push gate. I’ve also added cases that exercise reviews under `Off`, `Turn`, and `Push`; those checks are running.

Formatting passed. The checks are still compiling the controller tests. The revised cases cover reviews with automatic review disabled, while continuing to reject delegation tools for sessions that use `None`.
The daemon regression passed for all three triggers, including `Off` and `Turn`. Workspace Clippy also passed. The MCP checks and final crate suites are still running; no test failures have appeared.
The targeted daemon check is green. The remaining checks are waiting on the shared Cargo build lock while the worker tests compile; there are no failures to address so far.
The MCP contract checks passed too. I committed the follow-up as `10e9fd277` and requested review again. The complete core, worker, and controller suites are running in parallel with that review.

Fixed both findings in `10e9fd277`: `request_review` is now exposed and accepted regardless of the automatic review trigger.

Focused tests and Clippy passed. Review was requested again; full suites are running before push.
The remaining restriction is on managed children. I’ll extend on-demand reviews to those sessions and check the lifecycle guards so a child’s review can run safely alongside its parent.

There are two more guards behind the missing tools: children cannot register reviewer sessions, and message delivery rejects child senders. I’ll make messaging and review requests common to every role, allow reviewer registration for children, and preserve ordinary delegation restrictions. Nested reviewers will also retain the original container owner.

The changes are in place for every role. The regressions cover a child receiving its review verdict, persisted reviewer registration beneath a child, preservation of the original container owner, and messages carrying the child’s sender identity. Automatic turn reviews still skip children. Full validation is running.

Clippy is clean. The full test run is still compiling. The changes now cover both advertising the common tools to children and accepting their requests in the daemon, while preserving recipient ownership checks and ordinary delegation limits.

Validation found one failure in the new nested-reviewer case and a timeout in an existing continuation test. I’m checking both. I also found a worker-side restriction on reviews without a turn baseline; explicit commit reviews don’t need that baseline, so I’ve corrected the check and extended the real Git regression.

The nested-reviewer failure came from persisted-state validation. I’ve corrected it and added migration 108’s compatibility guard, since older daemons reject those relationships. The two failed tests and the real Git capture case are being rerun in isolation; the live store is untouched.
The isolated nested-reviewer test now passes, and Clippy is clean. The fix includes cycle rejection and compatibility protection for older daemons. The final full suites are running.

The full core, worker, and controller suites passed, including migration and child-review coverage. The continuation timeout passed on rerun and in the full suite. I’m committing the changes and requesting review again.

Committed as `2f18a1e20`. Managed children now receive messaging and review tools, with daemon support and compatibility protection.

Full tests, Clippy, and formatting passed. Review requested again; push is pending approval.

The reply restriction is real. I’ll make `send_message` work between sessions regardless of parentage, while keeping child lifecycle controls restricted to their owner. I’ll also test replies to child senders and messages from nested reviewers to their parent.

This comes from using child ownership rules for message recipients. I’ll separate those checks: messaging can reach any session that can receive work, while close still requires ownership. I’ll reuse the existing child wake handling so replies to parked children can be delivered.

Clippy passed. The updated regressions cover peer replies to children, replies that wake a parked child, and nested reviewers messaging their managed parent. They also check that messaging permission does not grant permission to close someone else’s child.

All seven focused message regressions passed, including the reply paths and parked-child wake. Formatting and Clippy passed too. The complete worker and controller suites are still running before I commit this follow-up.

The complete run is still compiling, with no failures reported so far. The fix reuses the existing child wake and capacity checks, and retains each message’s actual sender identity so replies can return to the right session.
The reply regressions passed again in the complete controller run. No failures have appeared; the remaining work is the upgrade matrix and worker checks.

The complete controller suite passed. The worker run found a description check for wording I shortened, plus an ACP adapter timeout. I’ll restore the required wording and rerun only those two tests. Upstream also advanced by one small macOS fixture fix; I’ll merge it before requesting review.

Both worker reruns passed, including the ACP test that timed out. Validation is complete. I’m committing the reply fix, merging the small upstream fixture change, and requesting review of the combined tree.

Committed the reply fix as `0b4ebb0ed` and merged upstream. Replies now reach managed children, including parked children and nested reviewers’ parents; lifecycle ownership checks remain intact.

Validation passed after targeted reruns. Review requested again before push.
Review is clean. I’m pushing the merged fix to `origin/master` now.
The push was rejected because another session advanced `master` during review. I’ll merge those changes into the current branch and request review of the merged tree before retrying.
Upstream moved during review, so the push was rejected. I merged it cleanly and requested review of merge commit `146cf220b`. I’ll retry the push when that review clears.
The merge review is clean. I’m retrying the push to `origin/master`.
Pushed successfully. I’m starting the macOS and Windows nightly checks because the fix also changes borrowed-container ownership and store compatibility.

Pushed `146cf220b` to `origin/master`. Common tools work across all session roles; delegation tools require `Mjolnir`. Child reviews and two-way messaging are fixed.

Validation and review passed. [Cross-platform checks](https://github.com/BrokkAi/mjolnir/actions/runs/41926108968) are running. The catalog fix takes effect with upgraded workers.
